result.note: Tests the composition and drivers of September 2026 CPI inflation and the RBI's October 2026 repo rate hike.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about retail inflation data for September 2026, released in October 2026:
items: Onion prices more than doubled year-on-year.
Tomato and potato prices declined year-on-year.
The RBI cited a deficient monsoon and renewed West Asia tensions among the causes of rising inflation.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. Onion prices rose 108.09% year-on-year, while tomatoes (-8.62%) and potatoes (-11.50%) fell. The RBI blamed a deficient monsoon and West Asia tensions, which pushed Brent crude in September 22% above its July average.
questions.source: Onion prices, which the official data shows more than doubled over the year, added to the pressure.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, after retail inflation reached a 22-month high, the Reserve Bank of India raised its repo rate to which level?
questions.explain: The RBI raised the repo rate by 0.25 percentage points to 5.5% on 7 October 2026. It expects inflation to average 6% in October to December and has ruled out near-term cuts.
questions.source: The RBI raised its repo rate by 0.25 percentage points to 5.5% on 7 October
